svg.title: The read floor in an Egres cluster: each node reports its lowest open read timestamp on heartbeat replies, the leader takes the minimum, proposes it in a snapshot, every replica applies it and compactions drop older versions
svg.desc: Three nodes list their open transactions and read timestamps. Follower 1 has a read at 1004 and an idle transaction past the maximum age, which is not counted; the leader has reads at 1020 and 1035; follower 2 at 1028. The leader heartbeats, the replies carry Tlow 1004 and 1028, and the leader takes the minimum of the snapshot target timestamp 1040, its own 1020 and the replies, Tsnap 1004. A snapshot entry with that floor goes through the Raft log, every node applies it and rejects reads below 1004: the counted reads continue and the aged-out transaction 4 is refused. A compaction of one row then drops the version at 950, keeps the version at 990 as the one a read at 1004 sees, and keeps the newer ones.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: EGRES · THE READ FLOOR · OPEN READS SET HOW FAR BACK A CLUSTER MUST REMEMBER
